promptText: Which hotel brands should an owner consider when converting an existing upper-upscale hotel asset in North America?
rawText:
This is a great and nuanced question. Here is a comprehensive guide to the hotel brands an owner should consider when converting an existing **upper-upscale asset in North America**, organized by franchisor family, brand type, and key owner considerations.

---

## 🏨 Hotel Brand Conversion Options for Upper-Upscale Assets in North America

### 📌 Why Conversions Are So Relevant Right Now


As a fast and affordable alternative to new construction, hotel conversions have been a way for owners and developers to quickly grow portfolio scale. Throughout the first half of 2024, hotel conversions remained highly desirable, reaching record project counts in the total U.S. hotel construction pipeline.
 
There has been an uptick in conversion-friendly brands, ranging from so-called "soft" brands that cater to boutique properties to more affordable offerings that can be a way for a hotel owner to tap into a bigger distribution platform.


---

## 🔷 MARRIOTT INTERNATIONAL — Upper-Upscale Conversion Brands


Marriott's upper-upscale brands run the gamut from resorts to trendy boutique hotels to the stylish W Hotel line.
 Key conversion-relevant brands include:

- **Autograph Collection** – 
Autograph Collection is a brand made up of 180 independent hotels around the world. These hotels are curated for guests who want forward-thinking experiences, as well as design-crafted spaces.
 It is among the most prominent soft/conversion brands in the upper-upscale segment.
- **Tribute Portfolio** – A soft brand option, part of 
Marriott's collection brands, which include the Autograph Collection, Tribute Portfolio, and Design Hotels.

- **Renaissance Hotels** – A full-service upper-upscale brand that appeals to lifestyle/discovery-oriented travelers.
- **Sheraton / Westin / Delta Hotels** – 
Delta Hotels has 105 hotels primarily in Canada, with ADR on the lower end of the upper-upscale tier. Delta competes with brands like DoubleTree and Crowne Plaza.


**Marriott's Strengths:** 
Marriott might be ideal if you want the widest array of brand options and a massive global engine behind you.


---

## 🔷 HILTON WORLDWIDE — Upper-Upscale Conversion Brands


Hilton has brands from luxury (Waldorf Astoria, LXR, Conrad) and lifestyle and full-service (Canopy, Curio, Signia, Hilton, DoubleTree, Embassy Suites) to focused and extended-stay properties.
 Key conversion-relevant brands include:

- **DoubleTree by Hilton** – 
Known for the warm chocolate chip cookie at check-in, DoubleTree properties offer full-service hospitality at a moderate price point. The brand is extensive with over 600 locations and provides a comfortable, welcoming experience.
 
DoubleTree was called out as one of Hilton's top conversion-driven brands, with 40% of Hilton's Q1 2025 openings being conversions.

- **Curio Collection by Hilton** – 
A collection of unique, independent hotels that join the Hilton ecosystem while retaining their individual identity. Curio properties range from historic boutique hotels to trendy urban properties, and are for travelers who want character and story with the security of Hilton Honors benefits.

- **Tapestry Collection by Hilton** – 
Similar to Curio but positioned at a slightly lower price point, Tapestry hotels are independent properties with unique personalities.

- **Embassy Suites by Hilton** – A strong all-suite, full-service upper-upscale brand suited for properties with suite-heavy configurations.
- **Signia by Hilton** – Hilton's convention/meetings-focused upper-upscale brand for large, event-driven properties.

**Hilton's Strengths:** 
Hilton offers a balance of scale and a century-long reputation for hospitality excellence.


---

## 🔷 IHG HOTELS & RESORTS — Upper-Upscale Conversion Brands

- **Crowne Plaza** – 
Crowne Plaza tailors its offerings for business travelers with round-the-clock dining options, fitness centers, meeting spaces, and amenities to help guests get a good night's sleep.
 It is IHG's workhorse upper-upscale brand and is conversion-friendly.
- **Vignette Collection** – IHG's soft/collection brand positioned in the upscale to upper-upscale segment. 
This collection brand sits somewhere between Vignette Collection and voco in the upscale and upper-upscale segment, where Hilton and Marriott already have several conversion brands.

- **Kimpton Hotels & Restaurants** – 
Kimpton, known for its boutique charm, delivers personalized service and distinctive design, creating memorable stays
 — well-suited for lifestyle hotel conversions in urban markets.
- **InterContinental Hotels & Resorts** – IHG's flagship luxury/upper-upscale brand, suited for landmark full-service properties. 
InterContinental offers luxurious accommodations in prime locations worldwide, catering to discerning travelers seeking elegance and sophistication.



IHG CEO Elie Maalouf reported 40% of the company's signings in Q1 2025 were conversions.


---

## 🔷 HYATT HOTELS CORPORATION — Upper-Upscale Conversion Brands

- **Hyatt Regency** – Hyatt's flagship full-service upper-upscale brand, ideal for large convention-adjacent or resort properties.
- **Unbound Collection by Hyatt** – 
Positioned just beneath true luxury, the Unbound Collection includes luxury and upper-upscale hotels that range from historic to ultra-modern and cosmopolitan to secluded.
 It is one of Hyatt's key soft/conversion brands.
- **Hyatt Centric** – A lifestyle-oriented full-service brand targeting urban locations and younger travelers.
- **Thompson Hotels / Alila / Andaz** – Hyatt's lifestyle and soft brand portfolio, which can work for distinctive upper-upscale conversion candidates.

**Hyatt's Strengths:** 
Hyatt, while smaller, provides an aspirational brand cachet and tends to dominate in the luxury boutique segment.


---

## 🔷 WYNDHAM HOTELS & RESORTS — Upper-Upscale Conversion Brands

- **Wyndham Grand** – Wyndham's upper-upscale full-service brand for resorts and city-center properties. 
With 25 distinct brands spanning the economy to upscale segments, Wyndham offers options for virtually every type of owner and market.


---

## 📊 Key Owner Considerations When Selecting a Brand

### 1. 🏗️ Property Improvement Plan (PIP) Costs

Franchise agreements typically run 20 years for new builds and 10 years for conversions, with extensive PIP requirements that can cost $10,000–$50,000 per room depending on property condition and brand tier.


### 2. 💰 Total Franchise Fee Burden

Fees typically include initial franchise rights, ongoing royalties, marketing contributions, and tech system charges, adding up to 8–12% of revenue in many cases.
 Specifically, 
luxury franchise fees grew 6.4% and upper-upscale fees grew 5.0%, while midscale fees declined 6.6% (CBRE, 2025).


### 3. 🎯 Loyalty Program Power (and Cost)

In 2024, loyalty program fees averaged 2.2% of rooms revenue and were highest at upper-upscale hotels. Properties that operate in this segment capture both corporate and group travelers, two types of frequent travelers that appreciate the benefits of loyalty programs.
 Additionally, 
loyalty program fees measured as a percentage of rooms revenue were greater at soft brand hotels compared to core brand hotels, indicating that loyalty program members are comfortable booking rooms beyond the primary brands within the major chains — good news for owners that opt to affiliate with a soft brand.


### 4. 🧩 Soft Brands vs. Hard Brands

The rise of soft brand collections (Marriott's Autograph Collection, Hilton's Curio Collection, IHG's Vignette Collection) has created a middle ground. These collections provide distribution system access and loyalty program integration without requiring the owner to build to a standardized prototype. The trade-off is a lower RevPAR premium at a similar or slightly lower fee structure. For lifestyle-oriented developers, soft brands offer the best of both worlds: distribution without standardization.


### 5. 📍 Market Positioning & Segment Alignment

Consider the relative market segment between both the old and new brands. Brand conversions which are staying within a similar market segmentation are likely to have less inherent risk than those which are further apart.
 
Align your choice with location type (urban core, suburban, interstate, airport, resort), physical layout, target demand segments (corporate, leisure, group, extended stay), and investment horizon and exit strategy.


### 6. 🔑 Key Money & Negotiation Leverage

Some brands offering key money also provide marketing, operational, and loyalty program support, which can enhance the property's long-term performance.
 
Understand that your leverage with the brand is greatest before signing a new franchise or management agreement.


### 7. 📈 RevPAR Performance Tracking

Brand affiliation can offer access to loyalty programs, favorable financing terms, and operational efficiencies, but the RevPAR performance of individual brands — and the consistency of that performance within a brand family — can meaningfully affect asset value over time. With performance gaps widening and new brands continuing to launch, it is more important than ever to assess whether a brand's positioning, fee structure, and customer mix are well aligned to generate profits across cycles and throughout the franchise agreement.


---

## 🗺️ Summary Brand Matrix

| Brand | Parent | Type | Best For |
|---|---|---|---|
| Autograph Collection | Marriott | Soft/Collection | Boutique, independent-spirited properties |
| Tribute Portfolio | Marriott | Soft/Collection | Lifestyle, independent properties |
| Renaissance | Marriott | Hard Brand | Full-service, lifestyle urban |
| Sheraton / Westin | Marriott | Hard Brand | Large full-service, corporate |
| DoubleTree by Hilton | Hilton | Hard Brand | Full-service, broad conversion appeal |
| Curio Collection | Hilton | Soft/Collection | Distinctive, character-driven properties |
| Tapestry Collection | Hilton | Soft/Collection | Independent properties, lower price point |
| Embassy Suites | Hilton | Hard Brand | All-suite, atrium-style properties |
| Signia by Hilton | Hilton | Hard Brand | Convention/meetings-centric properties |
| Crowne Plaza | IHG | Hard Brand | Business travel, urban/suburban |
| Vignette Collection | IHG | Soft/Collection | Upscale-to-upper-upscale independents |
| Kimpton | IHG | Lifestyle | Boutique urban lifestyle properties |
| InterContinental | IHG | Hard Brand | Landmark full-service properties |
| Hyatt Regency | Hyatt | Hard Brand | Large convention/resort properties |
| Unbound Collection | Hyatt | Soft/Collection | Distinctive upper-upscale properties |
| Hyatt Centric | Hyatt | Lifestyle | Urban lifestyle properties |
| Wyndham Grand | Wyndham | Hard Brand | Resort, city-center full-service |

The right brand ultimately depends on the property's physical configuration, location, target demand mix, existing competitive set, and the owner's investment horizon and return objectives. Engaging a hospitality advisor to run a formal brand study and negotiate PIP and franchise agreement terms is strongly recommended before committing to a flag.
